```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
bench <- read.csv("scores/benchmark_summary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
abl <- if (file.exists("scores/ablation_summary.csv"))
  read.csv("scores/ablation_summary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL
gt <- read.csv("ground_truth.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
ranking <- read.csv("scores/model_ranking.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bench$model <- factor(bench$model, levels = ranking$model)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
```

# 1. What was measured

Every dataset is a public perturbation experiment whose mechanism is
established independently of the transcriptome (drug target, receptor, or
knockout), so an interpretation can be scored against a ground truth rather
than against plausibility. For each dataset DEGinsight runs the same
pipeline — ORA against MSigDB Hallmark, ontology-constrained prompt, one LLM
call, validation — and the resulting mechanistic hypotheses are compared with
three pre-registered mechanism components per dataset.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(dataset = gt$dataset_id, GEO = gt$gse,
             perturbation = gt$perturbagen, system = gt$cell_type,
             `ground-truth components` = gsub("\\|", "; ", gt$gt_components),
             check.names = FALSE),
  caption = "Benchmark datasets and their pre-registered mechanism ground truth."
)
```

Three quantities are reported per run: **mechanism recovery** (fraction of
ground-truth components the interpretation recovers), **hallucination rate**
(fraction of cited pathways absent from both the input enrichment table and
the controlled vocabulary), and **cost** (tokens actually billed × published
per-token price).

# 2. Headline result

```{r}
agg <- aggregate(cbind(recovery_keyword, recovery_judge, hallucination_rate,
                       cost_usd, completion_tokens) ~ model, bench,
                 mean, na.rm = TRUE, na.action = na.pass)
knitr::kable(agg, digits = 3,
             caption = "Mean performance per model across all datasets.")
```

```{r}
per_ds <- aggregate(recovery_keyword ~ dataset + model, bench, mean,
                    na.action = na.pass)
ggplot(per_ds, aes(reorder(dataset, recovery_keyword), recovery_keyword,
                   fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip() + ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "mechanism recovery rate", fill = "model",
       title = "Recovery of the established mechanism, by dataset")
```

# 3. Does it hallucinate?

```{r}
ggplot(bench, aes(model, hallucination_rate, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) + facet_wrap(~ dataset) + ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "hallucination rate",
       title = "Cited pathways that exist in neither the input nor the vocabulary") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")
```

# 4. Cost-performance trade-off

```{r}
ggplot(agg, aes(cost_usd, recovery_keyword, label = model, colour = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1, size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(x = "mean cost per dataset (USD, log scale)", y = "mean recovery rate",
       title = "You get what you pay for — but the floor is high")
```

# 5. Ablation: prompt design

The ablation grid varies three factors that a user actually controls:
few-shot exemplar (on/off), number of pathways shown to the model
(5/10/20/30), and whether tissue context is supplied.

```{r}
if (!is.null(abl)) {
  m <- aggregate(cbind(recovery_keyword, hallucination_rate) ~
                   few_shot + top_n + tissue, abl, mean, na.action = na.pass)
  ggplot(m, aes(factor(top_n), recovery_keyword, colour = factor(few_shot),
                group = few_shot)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ tissue) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "pathways shown to the model (top_n)", y = "mean recovery rate",
         colour = "few-shot", title = "Ablation grid (all datasets pooled)")
  knitr::kable(m, digits = 3,
               caption = "Recovery and hallucination by ablation configuration.")
}
```

```{r}
if (!is.null(abl)) {
  cat("### Marginal effect of each factor\n\n")
  for (f in c("few_shot", "top_n", "tissue")) {
    cat("\n**", f, "**\n\n")
    print(knitr::kable(aggregate(recovery_keyword ~ abl[[f]], abl, mean,
                                 na.action = na.pass), digits = 3))
  }
}
```

# 6. Worked example

```{r}
ex <- bench[which.max(bench$recovery_keyword), ]
r <- readRDS(file.path("results",
  paste0(ex$dataset, "__", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", as.character(ex$model)), ".rds")))
cat("**", as.character(ex$model), "on", ex$dataset, "**\n\n")
for (h in r$interpretation$hypotheses) {
  cat("- **", h$name, "** — ", h$mechanism, "\n")
  cat("  * supported by: ",
      paste(unlist(h$supporting_pathways), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

# 7. Reproducibility

- Every LLM call is cached on disk keyed by a hash of prompt + model +
  temperature, so this report can be regenerated byte-identically without
  re-spending API budget (`R/cache.R`).
- `benchmark/00_fetch_geo.sh` downloads the exact archive versions used;
  byte sizes are pinned so a corrupted download fails loudly.
- All prompts, model versions and prices are recorded in
  `benchmark/results/*.rds` and `benchmark/models.csv`.
- Scoring is two-track: a deterministic synonym-aware keyword matcher (free,
  fully reproducible) and a model judge run **cross-model** — each output is
  judged by a different model than the one that produced it — to limit
  self-preference bias.

```{r}
cat("\n*Report generated:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"), "*\n")
```
